subject: Post-call recap & proposed MAP — FinPay evaluation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finpay.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@finpay.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed MAP — FinPay evaluation

Hi Alex & Priya,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation digging into the payments use case and latency/cost constraints. High-level recap and proposed next steps below so we have a single source of truth.

Call recap (brief):
- Primary goal: embed LLM-powered reconciliation and memo generation into FinPay's merchant dashboard; target p95 latency < 300ms for short prompts, burst to 1k qps during peak batch jobs.
- Key non-functional: security (SOC2 + audit logs), data residency (US), procurement windows (procurement + legal review).
- Decision criteria: accuracy on reconciliation prompts, predictable inference unit cost, SLA for peak times.

Stakeholder map (from today):
- Economic buyer: Priya Sharma (VP, Product) — owns ROI and go/no-go.
- Technical champion: Alex Turner (Eng Manager) — owns integration and testing.
- Security/Legal: TBD (procurement indicated contracting + security questionnaire).
- Procurement: ProcurementOps (we expect a 3-4 week standard review once security OK).

Proposed Mutual Action Plan (attached: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx)
- Week 1 (this week): Share MAP + SOC2 summary (attached).
- Week 2: Demo with Dylan (solutions engineer) to run through integration patterns + performance benchmarking test plan.
- Week 3: Security questionnaire & baseline evidence (SOC2 summary + logging options).
- Week 4-6: Eval period (pilot), run pilot prompts, share cost/latency dashboards; final procurement/terms.

Requests / asks for FinPay:
1) Please confirm the security reviewer contact (name + email) so we can route the questionnaire.
2) Confirm preferred pilot start window (earliest: Mar 2).
3) Share any additional decision criteria we should include in the MAP.

I'll loop in Dylan and Stephanie (CS) on the Scout demo and pilot plan.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOC2-Summary.pdf (pdf)
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@finpay.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed MAP — FinPay evaluation

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap. a few follow-ups from our side:

1) Security reviewer: that's Karan Patel (karan.patel@finpay.com) — I'll introduction him once you share the questionnaire.
2) Procurement timing: procurement has a sprint that ends Mar 12, so realistic earliest sign-off would be week of Mar 15 unless we can fast-track.
3) Decision criteria — Priya and I will add two more items:
   - Integration effort (estimated FTE weeks)
   - Ability to roll back model variants if quality regresses during pilot

Also — can Dylan run a short PoC run with a sample of our reconciliation prompts? We'll need to validate token cost estimates and p95 latency under our payload shapes.

If you can send the MAP as a Google Sheet and a high-level test plan, I'll pull in Karan and procurement.

Thanks,
Alex
Engineering Manager | FinPay
alex.turner@finpay.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finpay.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@finpay.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed MAP — FinPay evaluation

Alex — thanks, noted. I've uploaded the MAP as a Google Sheet and added a test plan draft and estimated effort column. Links and files below:

Links/attachments:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/finpay/redwood-map-v1 (Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx copied to Sheet)
- Attached: SOC2-Summary.pdf (summary of controls)

Quick answers:
- We can run the PoC using a 3-day benchmark run (Dylan will run locally with a 10k-sample prompt set). He'll measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens under your payload distribution.
- Rollback: Redwood supports model variant pinning + automatic fallback to last-known-good variant; we'll include a rollback runbook in the MAP.
- Procurement: We'll prepare a one-page SoW and standard security evidence pack for procurement review to shorten the cycle.

Proposed next calls:
- Friday, Feb 27 — 30m technical runbook + test plan with Dylan (suggest 10:00am PT).
- Week of Mar 2 — pilot kickoff (if procurement timelines allow).

Karan — looping you in to the thread so Dylan can share the security questionnaire and we can coordinate evidence.

Thanks — attaching the initial MAP (spreadsheet) for your review.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Marissa / Dylan — confirmed for Friday 10:00am PT. Karan is on the thread and will review the SOC2 summary ahead of the call.

Couple quick notes before the call:
- Procurement prefers a scope-limited pilot (3 weeks, NDA + data usage terms) — they'll draft the small SoW once security is satisfied.
- Priya asked that the MAP include specific success metrics (accuracy threshold on reconciliation, cost cap per 1k tokens).

See you Friday.
